QF.id: Taxation of Debt and Equity Products_13

question.text: Vikram, a senior citizen aged 62, has fixed deposits with two banks. Bank A pays him Rs.45,000 interest and Bank B pays Rs.30,000 interest during FY 2026-27. Per the current Section 194A senior-citizen threshold applicable for AY 2026-27, what is the total TDS deducted on his FD interest?

answer.text: Rs.7,500 (10% on total Rs.75,000 exceeding the threshold on aggregate)
Rs.2,500 (10% on Rs.75,000 minus a Rs.50,000 threshold applied on aggregate)
Nil, but only because the legacy Rs.50,000 threshold applies per bank
Nil, because each bank's interest is below the current Rs.1,00,000 senior-citizen Section 194A threshold per bank/branch

explanation.text: The Logic: Per the official Section 194A position applicable for FY 2026-27, the senior-citizen TDS threshold on interest from a bank, co-operative bank, or post office is Rs.1,00,000 per bank/branch (raised from the earlier Rs.50,000). Bank A pays Rs.45,000 (< Rs.1,00,000) and Bank B pays Rs.30,000 (< Rs.1,00,000), so neither bank triggers TDS. Total TDS = Nil. However, the aggregate interest of Rs.75,000 is fully taxable in Vikram's hands at slab rates. The Trap: The legacy Rs.50,000 senior-citizen threshold is the most common distractor; the threshold has been raised to Rs.1,00,000 for senior citizens. Aggregate-TDS framings (Options A and B) are wrong because TDS is computed by each deductor independently. Cross-Exam Context: NISM X-B and V-A test current Section 194A thresholds and the senior-citizen differential; Form 15H continues to apply where total income is below the basic exemption limit.
